items.title: Car salesman jailed 34 days, fined RM17,500 for cheating customers
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A car salesman was sentenced to 34 days in jail and fined RM17,500 by the magistrate's court here after pleading guilty to cheating three customers of their car purchase deposits totalling RM102,050. Khoo Chiang Chee, 38, was unable to pay the fine. Magistrate A. Shaarmini ordered him to serve between three and six months in jail in default of payment.

items.title: Woman brushing teeth behind wheel flashes middle finger before kicking auxiliary cop in groin at Glo Damansara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A woman who was allegedly brushing her teeth behind the wheel flashed her middle finger at an auxiliary police officer before getting out of her car and kicking him in the groin during a bizarre confrontation at Glo Damansara yesterday. The woman then managed to escape after a struggle with the 30-year-old officer, leaving police hunting for her following the incident in Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI). Brickfields district police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the officer approached the car to reprimand the woman and instruct her to move her vehicle.

items.title: UK's hard-right Reform hit by fresh scandal as racist views caught on camera
items.summary: LONDON: Britain's hard-right anti-immigration Reform UK party was hit by a fresh scandal on Thursday after party councillors and candidates were filmed in an undercover investigation using racist language. In another, a Reform member said his area had become "infested" with Asian families, calling them "absolute parasites." The broadcast followed Reform UK candidates and councillors during local elections in May and at four by-election campaigns in 2025 and 2026.

items.title: Netanyahu's main rival vows to defeat Hamas within 18 months if elected PM
items.summary: ISRAEL-GAZA BORDER: Israeli opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Miniter Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival in upcoming elections, vowed Thursday to defeat Hamas in Gaza if he becomes prime minister following the Oct 27 vote. He said he would achieve this either by implementing US President Donald Trump's ceasefire plan for Gaza, which provides for the gradual disarmament of Hamas and a transfer of power, or through "creative operations" by Israel's military aimed at destroying the Palestinian movement's military wing. Meanwhile, Israel's army chief said on Wednesday that the military was reinforcing troop levels "across all fronts", citing an increased risk of escalation as the country heads into elections this later month.

items.title: Selangor, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang schools stay open tomorrow amid haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow. In separate statements today, the State Education Departments (JPN) in the three states and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) encouraged all pupils, teachers, support staff (AKP), and school personnel to wear face masks. In Negeri Sembilan, the JPN said all outdoor activities — including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and open-hall events — must cease if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.

items.title: Motorists, motorcyclists caught in unusual Bandar Sunway traffic congestion
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Motorists were caught in traffic jams lasting up to an hour along several major roads around Bandar Sunway here today, with even motorcyclists struggling to get through the congestion. Several motorists took to social media to express their frustration over the unusually heavy traffic. Meanwhile, the Malaysian Highway Authority, in a Facebook post, reported slow-moving traffic on several highways around Bandar Sunway.

items.title: Wee refuses to retract statement on RM2.1bil ministry spending discrepancy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong has refused to retract his statement on the RM2.1 billion discrepancy involving the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW), insisting that he was speaking the truth. Wee, the Ayer Hitam MP, was responding to Kampar MP Chong Zhemin's demand that he retract the statement within 24 hours or face a referral to the Parliamentary Rights and Privileges Committee. Chong subsequently gave Wee 24 hours to retract his statement, warning that he would refer the Ayer Hitam MP to the Parliamentary Rights and Privileges Committee if he failed to comply.

items.title: 10 GOF personnel sacked over drug abuse, misconduct since last year
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Twenty-eight General Operations Force (GOF) personnel were found to have been involved in drug-related offences and disciplinary violations between last year and early this month, including personnel serving under Op Taring Wawasan along the Malaysia-Thailand border. He said 10 personnel had been dismissed from service, while investigations and disciplinary proceedings involving the remaining 18 were ongoing. Radzi said six personnel were dismissed last year, while four others were dismissed this year.

items.title: Still smiling at 117, Albanian may be world's oldest woman
items.summary: KUCOVA: At 117, Qamile Marra is not particularly concerned with proving she may be the world's oldest woman – or even persuading Albanian pension officials that she is not dead. For a woman born under Ottoman rule, who turned 36 a fortnight before the end of World War II and outlived Albania's communist dictatorship, her focus remains firmly on enjoying life. According to her birthdate as listed on several official documents – Aug 19, 1909 – Marra would be two days older than Britain's Ethel Caterham, recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's oldest living woman.

items.title: Sarawak gets RM545mil for Jendela 2 rollout, covers 350 sites - Fahmi
items.summary: KUCHING: The first stage of Phase 2 of the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela 2) rollout in Sarawak will cover 350 locations, with an allocation of RM545 million, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Meanwhile, Fahmi said Sarawak would have at least three submarine cable landing points under the Madani Submarine Cable (Salam) project. "Overall, the Salam project will involve 10 cable landing points nationwide," he said.

items.title: Schools in Selangor, Pahang, Negri Sembilan, Putrajaya to operate as usual tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All educational institutions under the Education Ministry in Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow. In separate statements today, the respective state education departments and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department encouraged pupils, teachers, support staff and other school personnel to wear face masks. In Negri Sembilan, the state education department said all outdoor activities, including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies and open-hall events, must stop if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.

items.title: Honeymoon hiccup: Malaysian couple’s car triggers Bangkok bomb scare
items.summary: BANGKOK, Oct 15 — A Malaysian couple on their honeymoon in Thailand sparked a security alert in Bangkok on Wednesday after their car was found parked in a prohibited area, prompting authorities to call in an Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team to inspect the vehicle. Metropolitan Police Bureau Commissioner Pol Lt Gen Siam Boonsom said the Malaysian-registered red car was found parked on the pavement along Sukhumvit 17 Lane in Bangkok’s Lumpini district, raising concerns amid heightened security for the ongoing IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings 2026. He said Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) officials spotted the vehicle during a patrol on Wednesday afternoon and alerted the authorities over concerns that it might contain hazardous materials.

items.title: 'No missing money': MP calls for clarity on RM2.1bil spending gap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenggara MP Manndzri Nasib has rejected allegations that RM2.1 billion was siphoned off from the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, saying the issue concerns financial management and governance. The ministry has said approved budget adjustments must be taken into account. Manndzri called on the Treasury secretary-general and the ministry's secretary-general to issue a joint statement clarifying the matter, warning against politicising what he described as a financial governance issue.

items.title: K9 unit steps up patrols at KLIA during peak hours
items.summary: SEPANG: Police have stepped up K9 patrols at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), particularly during peak hours, to strengthen security following several recent incidents. KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M. Ravi said patrols, previously conducted periodically, had been increased to bolster security at the airport. Ravi said patrols also took into account airport users' sensitivities, with handlers and their dogs deployed outside the terminal, including around entrances.

items.title: Selangor launches SA500 financing scheme for SMEs, NINE super app to consolidate services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Selangor today launched a financing initiative for businesses facing cash flow constraints alongside a super app intended to bring government services, payments and mobility options onto a single digital platform. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor Advance 500 (SA500) would help eligible companies and contractors undertaking state-related projects manage their cash flow, while the NINE Super App would make government services and everyday transactions more accessible to the public. Amirudin said access to financing remained a challenge for many businesses, with SA500 intended to ease cash flow pressures and help eligible companies sustain their operations.

items.title: Six masseurs seek RM10,000 to put Malay massage on world map in Italy
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Six Malaysian therapists who won international accolades in Paris last year will compete in the 'Two Unions Massage Championship' in Italy next month. The masseurs hope to showcase their skills in traditional Malay massage on the world stage. The competition features categories including traditional Malay and Asian massage, sports massage, facial massage, Western massage, aesthetic beauty massage, health massage and basic massage.

items.title: PRISM turns up the heat in Malaysia with Vincent Tan's Berjaya hotel deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prism, the premium hospitality business arm of OYO, is ramping up its expansion in Malaysia, teaming up with Tan Sri Vincent Tan-controlled Berjaya Group to bring ACES Hotel Kuala Lumpur under its Palette brand. The deal marks PRISM's latest move to build its presence in the country through partnerships with established property owners, as the hospitality sector positions itself to capture rising demand from international and domestic travellers. The partnership combines Berjaya Group's hospitality experience and local market knowledge with Prism's operating capabilities, allowing the hotel to tap a broader distribution network and reach more potential guests.

items.title: Menarabena Asia targets construction supply chain gaps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Menara Asia Sdn Bhd has launched Menarabena, a digital business-to-business platform aimed at improving procurement, access to construction materials and supply chain visibility. Menara Asia executive chairman Datuk Seri Saiful Nizam Mohd Yusoff said the platform was developed to help industry players make better procurement decisions. Saiful said the platform would also address order-tracking challenges faced by contractors.

items.title: AI worms, 'major' incident fears spur safety calls at industry summit
items.summary: FROM the spectre of refrigerator-infecting AI worms to warnings of "major" security incidents at the horizon, calls to prioritise safety in the development of artificial intelligence dominated an industry summit Wednesday. "There are more safety rules for a carton of milk than for AI. And we're going to need some new AI safety laws and rules."

items.title: Foreign student claims trial to stabbing ex-girlfriend, brother
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A university student from China pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court today to two charges of causing grievous hurt to his former girlfriend and her brother in a stabbing incident last month. However, she said if the court granted bail, it should be set at RM8,000 with two local sureties, and Chen should surrender his passport. Suhaila granted bail at RM8,000 with two local sureties and ordered Chen's passport to be impounded.

items.title: Seven seats in play, 21 firmly held: Zahid stakes out BN’s position in Melaka
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has said it will retain the 21 seats it won in the previous Melaka state election, leaving Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) component parties to negotiate over the remaining seven constituencies as discussions over electoral cooperation continue ahead of next month’s polls. BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was holding talks with PN’s core parties following the suspension of activities by the Opposition coalition, but made clear that BN had no intention of giving up the seats it currently holds. He said statements by PH leaders at both national and state levels indicated that the coalition had lost interest in working with BN for the Melaka election.

items.title: Pushing mega-projects, Hamzah Zainudin criticises Budget 2027 as ‘lacking vision’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today criticised Budget 2027 as “lacking vision”, arguing that the federal government’s spending plan lacks a long-term economic plan and relies heavily on short-term handouts. Hamzah (PN-Larut) cited the government’s failure to meet its target of RM90 billion in development expenditure for two consecutive years, arguing this indicates poor fiscal management that could fuel concerns about potential under-investment in infrastructure projects. Anwar tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for next year, of which some RM83 billion is earmarked for development.

items.title: Customs seizes RM162mil in drugs, including 460kg hidden in cemetery hut
items.summary: NILAI: The Customs Department seized 1,194.56kg of drugs worth RM161.667 million in four cases in Selangor and Perlis in September and October. Customs director-general Datuk Seri Amran Ahmad said the seizures comprised 753.91kg of methamphetamine, 33kg of cannabis and 407.65kg of heroin and cocaine combined. "On Sept 26, Customs inspected 16 boxes in the cargo section of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) destined for Australia and found 285 plastic packets containing white crystalline powder suspected to be drugs.

items.title: Hamzah: Extend fair representation to all parliamentary committees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The opposition wants fair representation under the Parliamentary Service Act extended to all parliamentary select committees, not just the Parliamentary Service Council. Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said that while the opposition supported the Act, improvements were needed to ensure its implementation was fair and comprehensive. Hamzah said fairness should apply to all parliamentary committees, not just the Parliamentary Service Council.

items.title: UMW Toyota sells 24,000 units in Q3, YTD sales top 60,800
items.summary: This brings its year-to-date sales to over 60,800 units, UMW Toyota said in a statejent today. UMW Toyota president Datuk Ravindran K said the third-quarter performance reflected Malaysians' continued trust in Toyota and the strength of its ownership experience. To encourage greater digital engagement, UMW Toyota has resumed its Toyota MY App campaign from Sept 14 to Dec 31.

items.title: Philippines politician allegedly funded jet carrying 521kg of drugs in Laos
items.summary: MANILA: Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) spokesperson Joseph Frederick Calulut on Thursday said investigators had verified that a politician from Mindanao allegedly financed the chartered private jet that carried 521 kilogrammes of suspected shabu worth PHP3.54 billion seized in Laos. He declined to disclose the politician's identity and the amount paid, said Philippine News Agency (PNA). Authorities said the shipment was reportedly bound for the Philippines.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Etiqa sees healthcare collaboration as key to containing medical costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 budget encourages greater collaboration among healthcare stakeholders, including insurance and takaful providers, to improve healthcare affordability and contain rising medical costs, said Etiqa Insurance and Takaful. Its group chief executive officer Kamaludin Ahmad said healthcare providers should build on the government's initiatives by developing more concrete measures to address rising medical costs and inflation, while strengthening the overall healthcare ecosystem. He also said that an emphasis on greater transparency through electronic medical records, which allow healthcare providers to access the same information, was among the key measures aimed at containing overall medical costs.

items.title: LBS Bina clinches double honours at Malaysia Developer Awards 2026
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: LBS Bina Group Bhd has secured two accolades at the Malaysia Developer Awards (MDA) 2026, strengthening its standing in Malaysia's property development sector through recognition of its market position and sustainability initiatives. In a statement, LBS Bina said the dual recognition highlights LBS' balanced approach to business growth, combining financial performance with responsible business practices, innovation and long-term value creation. LBS Group executive chairman Tan Sri Lim Hock San said the awards reflected the group's resilience, disciplined business approach and commitment to sustainable growth.

items.title: Malaysian-owned Taiton uncovers overlooked tungsten potential at Australia's Kingsgate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Taiton Resources Ltd, partly owned by Malaysian investors is uncovering fresh mineral potential at its Kingsgate project in New South Wales, Australia, after a review of decades-old exploration data revealed previously overlooked tungsten and antimony mineralisation alongside gold. The company said its review of historical shallow drilling identified 4.0 metres grading 0.20 per cent tungsten trioxide (WO₃) from 46 metres, including a 1.0-metre interval grading 0.47 per cent WO₃ from 49 metres. Historical soil sampling also outlined a coherent tungsten anomaly extending more than 100 metres, with peak concentrations of 920 parts per million (ppm).

items.title: Aafiyah receives RM5,000 in Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund aid
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Two-year-old Nur Faridah Aafiyah Muhammad Zamirul, who suffers from end-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) and internal organ complications since birth, has received RM5,000 in emergency aid from the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund. The aid, raised through public donations, was presented by Media Prima Berhad (MPB) Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) head Mohamad Farris Effendy Md Salim during a visit to the family's home in Desa Mentari here today. Mohamad Farris Effendy said the visit reflected MPB and The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Berhad's (NSTP) continued commitment to supporting communities facing health challenges and financial hardship.

items.title: Veterinary extension officers key to Malaysia’s food security, says deputy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — Veterinary extension officers play a crucial role in bridging government policies, the expertise of the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the farming community to boost livestock productivity and strengthen national food security. Themed “Veterinary Extension: A Driver for Productivity and Food Security”, the convention was also attended by Veterinary Services Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Noor Hisham Mohd Haron. The categories included Best State Veterinary Service, Best District Veterinary Service, Best Livestock-Based Industry Development Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project Poster, Best Veterinary Extension Project Video Presentation, Best Veterinary Extension Mentor/Officer and Best VetEC (Veterinary Extension Centre) Operation.

items.title: Musk calls on Zelenskyy to 'go' as Ukraine leader
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelenskyy to "go" as Ukraine's president, as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for the war-torn country. Ukraine accused the United States this week of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv's military response through changes to Musk's satellite system which it uses for communications. Musk said any disruption was the responsibility of the US government.

items.title: #NSTviral: Kuantan motorists caught off guard by roaming cattle
items.summary: KUANTAN: A herd of cattle created a disruption at a traffic light junction in Sungai Isap here after wandering through waiting vehicles and crossing against a red light. A 10-second video of the incident, recorded about 8pm yesterday, was posted by Facebook user Suhaila Zulkifli on the Warga Kuantan page, drawing mixed reactions from social media users. "Whose cow got loose near the Sungai Isap traffic light?

items.title: Drunk drivers may face asset seizure, extra jail for unpaid compensation – Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is formulating a mechanism to seize assets and impose additional jail terms on drunk or drug-impaired drivers who fail to pay compensation to road crash victims or the families of those killed. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the measures would ensure compensation orders under amendments to the Road Transport Act provide meaningful recourse, particularly when offenders claim they cannot afford to pay. Earlier, responding to Ahmad's question on amending the Road Transport Act to provide a legal basis for compensation to families of victims killed by drunk drivers, Loke said the Transport Ministry planned to table the amendments in parliament early next year.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM130M boost for local film, music, and creative content
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The allocation of more than RM130 million under Budget 2027 for the local film, music and creative industries is a timely move to boost the sector’s contribution to economic growth and talent development. MyCreative Ventures said in a statement today that the government’s support would help industry players nurture their talents, create high-quality content and build more resilient and sustainable creative businesses. “In an industry increasingly shaped by technology, digital content and global competition, creativity must extend beyond producing works to generating greater economic value,” it said.

items.title: Schools in Penang to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
items.summary: The Penang Education Department said all Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at monitoring stations across the state were below 150 as of 2pm today. In a statement, the department said it remained concerned about the safety and health of students amid the haze affecting the country. The department said it would continue to monitor air quality, adding that the safety, health and well-being of students and education personnel remained a priority.

items.title: Kepong knife attack: Chinese student charged with stabbing ex-girlfriend and her brother
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A 20-year-old Chinese national university student pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of causing grievous hurt by stabbing his former girlfriend and her younger brother with a knife last month. Chen Jun is accused of causing grievous hurt to Leong Kai Ting, 21, and her younger brother, Leong Shun Jie, 18, by stabbing them both with a knife capable of causing death. Chen Jun appeared in court in a wheelchair.

items.title: Pakistan school roof collapse kills 27 students, one teacher
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: At least 27 students, most of them below the age of 13, and one teacher were killed on Thursday when a school roof collapsed while they were being taught in class in Pakistan's Peshawar city, authorities said, and feared the death toll could rise. Rescue teams were working to shift bodies and the injured to hospitals, government official Bilal Faizi said. A rescue official said the roof of a higher floor collapsed on the roof of the first floor of the building which in turn collapsed on students in classes.

items.title: 'It's like she's still with us' – Irene Sofiya's grandfather
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Nearly two weeks after 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal was murdered, her family continues to grieve, missing her laughter and voice. Her 65-year-old grandfather, Khyar Abas, said he still felt her presence in every corner of their home. He said the loss was particularly painful as he had been closest to Irene Sofiya, whom he raised following her mother's death eight years ago.

items.title: Perikatan ‘almost 100pc’ certain of Melaka election alliance, but Takiyuddin keeps potential partners under wraps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is almost certain to forge an alliance with other political parties ahead of the Melaka state election, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today, although he stopped short of revealing who its potential partners might be. Takiyuddin did not disclose which parties PN was negotiating with or whether the talks involved BN. He said discussions over seat allocations were already under way, both with potential allies and among PN’s own component parties.

items.title: Zetrix AI pledges cooperation as police, MACC probe unpaid RM314m collections
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Zetrix AI Bhd will fully cooperate with authorities in an ongoing joint investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). The company was responding to a query from Bursa Malaysia Securities dated Oct 14 regarding a media report entitled "Police say six witnesses questioned in probe into MyEG, Zetrix AI” published by The Edge Malaysia on Oct 13. Zetrix AI said it would communicate any material developments through official announcements.

items.title: Court hears charges against former UKM director accused of RM3.12m contract abuse
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — A former director of an education centre at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of abusing his position to secure employment contracts worth RM3.12 million in 2022. Datuk Prof Muhammad Hussin, 64, a retiree, entered the plea after the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. According to the charges, Muhammad, a member of Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB), allegedly abused his position to secure two contracts worth RM1.2 million and RM1.92 million respectively to manage the Master of Education programme through UKM’s Faculty of Education.

items.title: Sarawak man finds RM1b in bank account, asks ChatGPT to count the zeros — only to discover it’s a glitch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — When a Sarawak clinic manager opened his banking app and discovered a mysterious 10-digit balance, he did what some people might do when faced with an eye-watering number: he asked ChatGPT. But for Wan Muhammad Fairus, 33, whose account should have contained less than RM1,000, his unexpected brush with billionaire status was over almost as quickly as it began. According to Berita Harian , the father of four from Samariang, Kuching, was in his bedroom preparing to make a banking transaction when he stumbled upon the extraordinary balance.

items.title: Health Ministry races to stock aerochambers and nebulisers as haze drives surge in respiratory cases
items.summary: He said the ministry had also activated the National Haze Operations Room on Sept 4 and was closely monitoring three main health conditions, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, through 78 sentinel healthcare facilities. “Through the Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), the ministry is stepping up public health measures in response to rising Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and deteriorating air quality caused by open burning,” he said when replying to a question from Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah). Dzulkefly said monitoring at 78 sentinel healthcare facilities nationwide showed that URTI cases surged by 167.21 per cent to 7,065 in epidemiological week 36, compared with 2,644 cases the previous week, due to deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Teenagers among 14 charged in Gurun murder, victim allegedly tortured before body found near golf club
items.summary: The accused are Muhammad Asyraaf Muhammad Zaidi, 20; Muhammad Azrul Rahimi Muhamad Yusri, 18; Ahmad Izzul Irfan Ridduan, 21; Muhammad Rhahimy Abdul Rashid, 19; Yusman Hakimi Yusmezal, 24; Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain Khairol Fais, 21; and Muhammad Aiman Riduwan Abdullah, 21. The other accused are Ahmad Aiman Danial Ahmad Wizam, 21; Muhammad Adam Haris Rosdan, 21; Muhammad Muqkriz Azizan, 21; Muhammad Adam Iqbal Mohd Wazir, 19; Syafiq Afif Syarafuddin Abd Ghapar, 23; and two teenagers aged 16 and 17. Only three of the accused, Muhammad Azrul Rahimi, Ahmad Izzul Irfan and Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain, were represented by lawyer Mohamad Ashraf Ahmad Sohaimi.

items.title: Prisons Department probes Kajang jail after NGO flags water shortages, dirty food trays and poor hygiene
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Prisons Department is investigating allegations by a non-governmental organisation (NGO) concerning water supply disruptions, sanitation facilities and food provision at Kajang Prison. The department said it consistently prioritised inmates’ welfare, health, hygiene and safety, including the provision of basic necessities, in accordance with existing regulations and procedures. Earlier today, Lawyers for Liberty, in a statement, raised concerns over alleged water shortages and unsanitary conditions at Kajang Prison.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng urges Malaysia to sue Indonesia over haze if Jakarta rejects Asean firefighting task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged Malaysia to consider legal action against Indonesia to seek compensation for the worsening transboundary haze crisis if Jakarta refuses to cooperate with a proposed permanent Asean firefighting task force. Lim said the recurring crisis, which has forced schools to close and disrupted livelihoods, could no longer be treated as an annual inconvenience, calling for a coordinated regional response to tackle forest and land fires at their source. The call comes as Malaysia continues to grapple with deteriorating air quality caused by smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia, with 34 of the country’s 68 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today.

items.title: Apology on Threads but not in newspapers: Man faces contempt proceedings in Christy Ng defamation case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A man ordered to pay fashion entrepreneur Christy Ng and her company RM180,000 in damages over defamatory social media posts is facing contempt of court proceedings after allegedly failing to publish apologies in newspapers as directed by the High Court. The High Court in Kuala Lumpur has fixed Monday to hear a committal application filed by Ng and Christy Ng Sdn Bhd against J Vikneshvra Rau, Berita Harian reported. On September 15, the High Court granted Ng and her company permission to initiate committal proceedings against him for alleged contempt of court.

items.title: Fatal crash drivers could face asset seizure if compensation to victims unpaid, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Proposed amendments to federal road transport laws could empower courts to seize the assets of drivers convicted of fatal crashes if they fail to pay court-ordered compensation to victims’ families, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Parliament today. The government is currently drafting amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) to establish a mandatory compensation mechanism for victims and next-of-kin affected by reckless driving and driving under the influence (DUI). Replying during Question Time, Loke revealed that the ministry is exploring asset seizure alongside tougher secondary penalties, such as heavier fines or extended prison sentences to prevent convicted drivers from evading financial restitution.

items.title: Sultan Ibrahim attends day two of 273rd Conference of Rulers
items.summary: The meeting was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. Also in attendance were the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail; Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; Sultan of Kedah, Al-Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah; and Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah. Also present were the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim.

items.title: Defence lawyer denies family statements in Irene Sofiya case, warns against fabricated social media posts
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 15 — The defence counsel representing the 16-year-old student charged with the murder of classmate Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal today disavowed any statements or apologies purporting to be from the boy’s family. Lawyer Mohd Azlan Shah Mohd Allias stressed that the accused teenager’s family has maintained complete silence throughout the investigation, never releasing statements or publishing posts across any digital channels. Mohd Azlan was addressing viral claims alleging that the accused boy’s family had sought an out-of-court meeting with Irene Sofiya’s relatives.

items.title: Malaysia’s births fall 4.5pc in 2025 as fertility rate drops to 1.5 children per woman
items.summary: The crude birth rate (CBR) also recorded a decrease from 12.2 births in 2024 to 11.6 births per 1,000 population in 2025. Malays recorded the highest CBR with 14.9 births, while Chinese remained to record the lowest CBR with 5.0 births per 1,000 population in 2025,” DOSM said in a statement. The TFR for Indians remained unchanged at 1.1 children, while Chinese recorded the lowest TFR, declining from 0.9 children to 0.7 children in 2025.

items.title: F1 return: Youth and Sports Ministry to table cost-benefit evaluation to Cabinet next month
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Sports and Youth Ministry is set to present its assessment on whether or not Malaysia should resume hosting the Formula 1 Grand Prix to the Cabinet next month, its minister Mohd Taufiq Johari told Parliament this morning. The ministry was mandated to lead an inter-ministerial F1 assessment committee formed to evaluate the projected costs and return on investment for the country, the minister revealed, following revived interest to resume hosting the grand prix after the overwhelming turnout at the race in Sepang. The announcement comes on the heels of Sepang International Circuit’s (SIC) successful hosting of the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix earlier this month, marking F1’s first return to Malaysia in nine years.

items.title: Loke: CAAM audit identified minor issues prior to fatal Sarawak chopper crash, but found no direct link
items.summary: Transport Minister Anthony Loke, addressing Parliament today, said the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) recorded three audit findings and three observations during a surveillance audit from September 1 to September 4, including issues of manpower planning calculations, maintenance handover records, and emergency response documentation. “The scope of the surveillance audit encompassed aspects of maintenance organisation compliance, manpower management, maintenance control, management of aircraft equipment and components, as well as the Safety Management System (SMS),” Loke said during Question Time. “The audit findings on Layang-Layang’s maintenance organisation recorded three audit findings and three observations,” he added.

items.title: Fatal Jalan Kuching pile-up: 24-year-old BYD driver claims trial to causing child’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A 24-year-old bank assistant sales manager claimed trial at the Magistrate's Court here today to three traffic charges, including causing the death of a five-year-old girl in a six-vehicle collision along Jalan Kuching last weekend. On the primary charge, Goh is accused of causing the death of Asiah Ahmad Syahir by recklessly driving his BYD Seal electric vehicle along Jalan Kuching, heading towards Segambut, at around 3.44pm on Oct 10. The charge, framed under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving, carries a prison sentence of between five and 10 years, a fine ranging from RM20,000 to RM50,000, and a minimum five-year disqualification from holding a driving licence upon conviction.

items.title: TNB: Malaysia needs massive power generation investment now
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) said there is a need for substantial investment in power generation and grid modernisation to support Malaysia’s changing energy mix while maintaining affordable, reliable and secure electricity supply. The priorities include expanding solar generation supported by energy storage and developing new combined-cycle power plants designed to be hydrogen-ready, he said. The investment supports grid strengthening and modernisation to accommodate rising electricity demand and greater integration of renewable energy.

items.title: Johor student charged with the murder of Form Four classmate Irene Sofiya
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 15 — A 16-year-old schoolboy was charged in the Magistrate's Court here today with the murder of his classmate, Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, whose body was discovered inside a secondary school hall in Yong Peng earlier this month. No plea was recorded from the teenager, whose identity is protected by law as a minor, because murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court. According to the charge sheet, the accused is alleged to have murdered 16-year-old Irene Sofiya in Dewan Sri Tanjung at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Dato' Seth in Yong Peng between 2.30pm and 4.00pm on Oct 3.

items.title: BYD Seal driver hauled to court over six-vehicle Jalan Kuching crash that killed toddler
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The 24-year-old driver of a BYD Seal involved in a fatal six-vehicle pile-up along Jalan Kuching last weekend was brought to the court complex here today to face three traffic offences, including causing the death of a five-year-old girl. Handcuffed and dressed in a green shirt, the suspect was escorted by traffic police personnel to the Kuala Lumpur magistrate's court this morning, NST reported. He is also set to face charges under Section 42(1) for reckless and dangerous driving, alongside Section 52(1) for failing to stop and report a road crash.

items.title: Choking haze sweeps Malaysia: 34 stations unhealthy, zero stations record good air
items.summary: Data from the DOE dashboard at 9.30am showed that 34 out of 68 stations registered Air Pollutant Index (API) readings between 101 and 200, marking a steady deterioration from 28 stations yesterday afternoon and 27 yesterday morning. The remaining 34 stations sat in the moderate tier, while the two stations that still recorded good air quality a day earlier slipped out of the bracket. Selangor logged six unhealthy stations, with Shah Alam touching 179, Banting 170, Petaling Jaya 168, and Kuala Selangor 161.

items.title: MinDef enters cooperation with HR Ministry on veteran employment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Defence (MinDef) is strengthening its commitment to the welfare and future of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel and veterans through the MyBakat Veteran initiative, which aims to benefit more than 15,000 people by 2030. Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiative underscores MinDef’s new approach to ensuring that MAF personnel receive support not only during their service but are also better prepared to pursue a second career after retirement. He said the ministry is placing greater emphasis on aligning military skills and experience with industry requirements to broaden job opportunities for MAF personnel and veterans.
